title: More Than 67.32 Percent of the Zeta Zeros Are Simple and on the Critical Line
description: Paper (REVTeX source and PDF) and verification code. We prove that more than 67.32 percent of the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function, counted with multiplicity, are simple and lie on the critical line: liminf N_0^s(T,2T)/N(T,2T) >= (125000/124111)(H - 7999/2000000) = 0.6732896395, where H = 0.6725007 is the Montgomery-Taylor constant (release 1.0.0 gave 0.6731133552, release 1.1.0 gave 0.6731985970 and release 1.2.0 gave 0.6732133974). The ingredients are a sharp bound for the largest eigenvalue of the overlap matrix of zeros at mutual distance at least 11/20, which lets long blocks of zeros be used in full, and a window inequality for ten consecutive zeros in which every pair and every gap carries its own weight, chosen by linear programming. The inequality F >= 889/125000 is verified by branch and bound in interval arithmetic with two lower bounds on a box, one from a table of kernel bounds on cells and one from a second-order Taylor expansion over tables of the kernel and its first two derivatives, all computed in 128-bit ball arithmetic (1,424,333,714 nodes, under three minutes on four threads). No weights for ten zeros give more than 0.6732908, and no window length or weights lift the method above 0.67357. The Riemann hypothesis is not proved and the result does not bear on it. The route was found with the learn-from-failure protocol of the BLLM engine Anaxia (creelie/eBLLM, release 3.1.1, doi:10.5281/zenodo.23484395).
